chunks: Abul ‘Abbās Al-Razzāz narrated to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb narrated to us from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl, from Al-Khaybari, from Ḥusain ibn Muḥammad Al-Qummi, who said:

Abul Ḥasan, Mūsā (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)) said: The minimum reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) by the shores of the Euphrates (River) while knowing his rights and believing in his sanctity and Wilāyah is that all of their past and future sins will be forgiven.

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ: Imam Husain ibn Ali (a.s.), the grandson of the Prophet
key_terms.زَائِرُ: Visitor (specifically in the context of religious pilgrimage)
key_terms.شَاطِئِ الْفُرَاتِ: Shores of the Euphrates River, a key location for Husain's shrine

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for performing Ziyarah to Imam Husain by the Euphrates?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) highlights the profound spiritual efficacy of visiting Imam Husayn at the banks of the Euphrates, linking physical pilgrimage with deep gnosis (ma'rifah) of their rights and authority. The promise of comprehensive forgiveness—encompassing both past and future sins—underscores the concept of *sabr* and *tawassul* through the Ahl al-Bayt, a central theme in Shia devotional practice. This narration serves as a key textual basis for the belief that Ziyarah is not merely a ritual but a transformative act of worship that expiates sins through divine grace.
